narration:
November 2026.
Jensen Huang resigns as CEO of Nvidia, the company he built over 33 years.
In one week, nearly half a trillion dollars of its value disappears.
Every headline says the same thing.
Affairs.
One with a woman US officials suspected of being a Chinese spy.
But here's the strange part.
Washington had reportedly known about her for a year.
And did nothing.
So what really brought down the most powerful CEO in tech?
It starts with an email.
Nvidia makes the chips behind almost every AI you've used.
It's worth over $5.5 trillion.
And Nvidia is Jensen.
Around 60 executives report straight to him.
No number 2.
Then Jensen writes to his staff:
"I owe my family and all of you an apology.
I was unfaithful to my wife.
I'm committed to supporting America's national security." National security?
Why say that?
Because the woman was Alice Huang.
No relation.
Her company was one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia.
And according to US intelligence claims,
China's spy agency had sent her to get close to him.
A honeypot.
3 days later, The New York Times reported a second relationship,
with an executive who reported directly to Jensen.
The board met that night.
By morning, he was out.
Then Reuters reported a third woman.
33 years.
Over in 4 days.
A billionaire, a spy, a honeypot.
Case closed.
Except 2 things don't fit.
First, the spy.
Alice had a husband who'd known Jensen for 10 years.
The Wall Street Journal reported he introduced them and called
his wife "Jensen's personal secretary." That's not how honeypots work.
Singapore police never investigated her for spying.
Second, the timing.
The president had reportedly been briefed about her a year earlier.
Nobody stopped Jensen.
Nobody even told him.
So forget the affair.
Follow the chips.
Washington, 2022.
"Mr.
Huang,
your best chips don't go to China anymore." "But we own 95%
of that market." "Sounds like your problem." Jensen fought it for years.
The best chips stayed banned.
3 years in, he said Nvidia's China share went from 95% to 0.
Lose a market that big and you're supposed to shrink.
Nvidia didn't.
One quarter: $44 billion, up from 26 a year before.
But the fine print had something odd.
Right behind America in Nvidia's country table: Singapore.
Smaller than New York.
Reportedly over a fifth of Nvidia's revenue.
Is every grandma in Singapore running a data center?
Nvidia's answer: Singapore is just where the invoices go.
So are banned chips being snuck into China?
Jensen laughed it off.
Our systems weigh 2 tons and cost $3 million.
Nobody carries that through an airport.
Okay.
Let's go look.
Singapore, 2025.
Megaspeed, one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Asia.
Nearly $5 billion of Nvidia hardware in 3 years.
"Where is everybody?" "This is everybody." 2 people on a workday.
Its Australian branch was reportedly run by a 29-year-old who worked at a newsstand.
5 months after the chip ban,
a British Virgin Islands shell bought the company and renamed it.
That shell was Hang Lee Limited, reportedly Alice Huang's Chinese name.
Employees later said she still ran it.
Its job: buy Nvidia chips, put them in Malaysian data centers,
rent out the power.
Legal.
Malaysia isn't China.
But first year, 0 revenue.
A year later, $3 billion in assets.
Where's the money from?
Short seller Culper Research alleged it came from a
Singapore company that paid over $4 billion in advance.
Its parent: Alibaba.
Chinese money in.
Nvidia chips out.
"Why are the servers still in their boxes?" "We're still setting
up." Nobody buys millions in chips to leave them boxed.
Unless they're not staying.
US investigators allege around 240,000 banned Nvidia chips
went through Megaspeed's shell companies into China.
So this was never just a love story.
Alice got access.
China got the chips.
Nvidia got a customer that never stopped buying.
Everybody wins.
Except Washington.
So why did nothing happen?
Officials pushed to blacklist Megaspeed.
Commerce never did.
It reportedly added no one for over a year,
its longest gap in 18 years.
Its agents were building a case, then Nvidia's lawyers got involved, and it stalled.
Because Jensen was one of Donald Trump's favorite guests.
A reported $1 million Mar-a-Lago dinner.
Trips abroad with Trump.
A $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.
Marco Rubio's team reportedly wrote a classified memo warning she might be a spy.
Trump still took Jensen to Beijing.
That was the shield.
Then America voted.
The president's party lost Congress.
The memo leaked.
Congress summoned Jensen.
A second affair broke.
Then a third.
Jensen Huang resigned.
"An affair?
He washed dishes at Denny's and built all this." "Banned chips flowed
into China through her company while he said there was no smuggling.
And he dated someone who reported to him." Allegedly.
He hasn't been charged with anything.
So who runs the company AI depends on?
There's no second Jensen.
Except everyone is replaceable.
Steve Jobs died, and Apple got bigger.
Building Nvidia was extraordinary.
But once nobody can replace you, nobody can stop you.
Follow the channel for the next one.
Too important to fire.
Too rich to refuse.
Too connected to touch.
Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.

research.summary: The linked video’s central event is real: NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO, and board member in November 2026 after revelations about extramarital relationships and scrutiny over his connection to Alice Huang, a Singapore-based technology executive whom U.S. officials reportedly suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. However, several details in the supplied brief require correction or qualification. The company said its board had no reason to believe that NVIDIA secrets or national security information were compromised, and the alleged espionage claims remained unproven. The financial impact was larger than the brief states: Reuters reported approximately $550 billion in NVIDIA market value was erased during the week of November 9–12, 2026, while AP later reported a loss of about $735 billion since the disclosures. The strongest evidence points to a combined corporate-governance, national-security, export-control, and leadership crisis—not a proven spy operation.

claims.claim: NVIDIA announced on November 12, 2026 that Jensen Huang had resigned immediately as president, chief executive officer, and a member of the board. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO, and Harvey C. Jones became board chair.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition

claims.claim: Huang founded NVIDIA in 1993 and had led the company for 33 years before his resignation.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition

claims.claim: NVIDIA’s board opened an independent investigation on November 8, 2026 into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board explicitly said it had no reason to believe that national security or NVIDIA secrets had been compromised.
claims.source_title: Statement From NVIDIA Board of Directors

claims.claim: NVIDIA published a message from Huang on November 8, 2026 in which he apologized to his family and colleagues and acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA News Archive — A Message to Our Company

claims.claim: Reuters reported that the U.S. intelligence allegation concerned Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, and that U.S. intelligence officials believed she had passed information to the Chinese government. Reuters also said it could not independently verify the allegation.
claims.source_title: Trump’s close ties to Nvidia’s Huang scrutinized after foreign intelligence concerns

claims.claim: The supplied brief’s claim that the board acted after a second relationship was reported is broadly supported by contemporaneous reporting, but the exact identity and employment details of every alleged additional partner should not be stated as settled fact without a direct primary source.
claims.source_title: Jensen Huang steps down and Nvidia shares drop

claims.claim: NVIDIA’s market value fell by approximately $550 billion during the week ending November 12, 2026, according to Reuters. Bloomberg reported that the company’s market capitalization fell below $4 trillion after Huang’s resignation.
claims.source_title: Retail buyers limit Nvidia stock rout

claims.claim: AP later reported that NVIDIA had lost about $735 billion in market value since disclosures about Huang’s affairs and his ties to the alleged Chinese spy. These figures describe different measurement windows and should not be presented as contradictory exact totals.
claims.source_title: World markets mostly drop as AI stocks remain under pressure

claims.claim: The phrase “95% market share to 0%” is a real quotation attributed to Huang in a transcript of a 2025 discussion about NVIDIA’s China business and U.S. export controls. It should be framed as Huang’s characterization, not as an independently audited current market-share measurement.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang on AI: The Next Frontier of Growth

claims.claim: NVIDIA’s filings and Singapore government statements support the point that revenue billed to Singapore did not necessarily mean the physical chips were consumed there. NVIDIA reported that more than 99% of controlled data-center compute revenue billed to Singapore was for orders from U.S.-based customers in the relevant fiscal 2026 reporting period; Singapore’s trade ministry separately said physical delivery of NVIDIA products to Singapore represented less than 1% of overall revenue.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Form 10-Q; Singapore Ministry of Trade and Industry statement reported by CNA
claims.published_or_updated: NVIDIA filing dated 2025; Singapore statement updated February 18, 2025

claims.claim: Megaspeed was suspected by U.S. authorities of helping Chinese companies obtain restricted NVIDIA AI chips, but the available reporting describes an investigation or suspicion, not a proven criminal finding. Megaspeed said it cooperated with U.S. Commerce Department inspections and undertook an inventory and export-control review.
claims.source_title: The Latest: Trump says he plans to talk about war in Ukraine during meeting with Xi and Putin

claims.claim: The U.S. government moved on November 16, 2026 to require licenses for advanced-chip sales to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil because officials considered those routes at elevated risk of diversion to China. This policy development strengthens the export-control context of the NVIDIA scandal but does not prove that NVIDIA or Megaspeed illegally diverted chips.
claims.source_title: Trump administration moves to block China from indirect access to American AI technology

claims.claim: The allegation that Washington knew about Alice Huang for roughly a year is reported, but it remains an account attributed to news reports and officials rather than a publicly released government finding. The Atlantic reported that President Trump was reportedly warned in 2025 and again in 2026, while Reuters reported renewed scrutiny of the administration’s relationship with Huang.
claims.source_title: China’s Intelligence Coup in the AI War

claims.claim: NVIDIA’s official materials identify the company as founded in 1993, led by Jensen Huang until his November 2026 resignation, and focused on accelerated computing and AI infrastructure. The brief’s wording that Huang started the company in “Adenis” is an error; the company was founded in the United States by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA in Brief

core_fact.fact: The topic video concerns NVIDIA’s November 2026 leadership crisis: NVIDIA’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation effective immediately on November 11, 2026, and the company announced the transition publicly on November 12, 2026, after reports about his extramarital relationships and alleged ties to a Chinese intelligence operation involving Alice Huang. The intelligence allegation was not established as fact; NVIDIA said it had no reason to believe that company secrets or national security information had been compromised.

metadata.title: NVIDIA Scandal Explained: Affairs, Chips, and China
metadata.description:
Free guide to this video (steps and every source): https://studio.golidee.com/guides/golide-long-2026-11-17.pdf

Jensen Huang built Nvidia into the most valuable company in the AI boom. Then, in November 2026, he resigned after reports of affairs, a suspected Chinese intelligence connection, and questions about Nvidia chips reaching China through Singapore-based Megaspeed.

This video follows the money, the export-control investigation, the political connections, and the unanswered questions surrounding Nvidia’s sudden leadership crisis. It also examines whether the affair was the real cause of Huang’s downfall—or just the story that exposed a much bigger problem.

#JensenHuang #Nvidia #NvidiaScandal #AIChips #ChinaTech #ExportControls #TechNews #GOLIDE
